draft.briefing: Hey, you're at Malampuzha! The dam here was finished in 1955, and its gardens became one of Kerala's favourite day trips. Look for the giant Yakshi sculpture, a famous piece of modern art.
draft.hungryLine: Food here is snacky: ice cream, fried bites and tea around the gardens.

moodReplies.show-me-around: Walk the gardens, see the Yakshi sculpture, then ride the ropeway over the park.
moodReplies.somewhere-to-chill: Sit by the reservoir in the evening as the garden lights come on.
moodReplies.surprise-me: The Yakshi, a reclining nude woman, caused a storm when Kanayi Kunhiraman made it in 1969.

legends.title: The sculpture that shocked Kerala
legends.body: Kanayi Kunhiraman made the Yakshi in 1969. People argued about her for years, and now she's a landmark.

legends.title: Built for Hyder Ali
legends.body: The fort in town was built in 1766 for Hyder Ali of Mysore, Tipu Sultan's father.

tips.title: Come late afternoon.
tips.body: The gardens are lit up in the evening.

tips.title: Weekends are busy.
tips.body: Go on a weekday if you can.

story.title: The Palakkad Gap
story.body: Palakkad sits in a gap in the Western Ghats, the easiest way into Kerala from Tamil Nadu.

story.title: A fort
story.body: Hyder Ali built Palakkad Fort to control the gap.

story.title: The dam
story.body: The Malampuzha dam was finished, bringing water to Palakkad's rice fields.

story.title: The Yakshi
story.body: Kanayi Kunhiraman's Yakshi gave the gardens a famous, and controversial, artwork.

story.title: Your turn
story.body: Gardens, Yakshi, ropeway, then the fort. Tell me what you thought of her.
